meta.title: Paradox Origin - 1
meta.description: All that is needed for a stranger to become a comrade is for the two of you to be protecting the same person.

spans.text: Professor, what's the status of the Entropic? Did it... Hng!

units.rawText: Hey, hey! Worry about yourself before you worry about the Professor.
units.displayText: Hey, hey! Worry about yourself before you worry about the Professor.

spans.text: Hey, hey! Worry about yourself before you worry about the Professor.

units.rawText: You used too much operands just to protect me. You need to take a good rest.

units.rawText: There's no need to worry any longer, Sangoma and I have handled it.

spans.text: Bonneville, could I ask you to do something?

units.rawText: You want me to relay your message, right? No problem, leave it to me.

units.rawText: Thank you, Bonneville.

units.rawText: ...Persicaria, Sangoma, can you both come here? I want to confirm something with you.

spans.text: ...Persicaria, Sangoma, can you both come here? I want to confirm something with you.

units.rawText: It was an urgent situation, but I still got a chance to take a picture of the replica, and also discovered the reason why it felt so off-putting.
units.displayText: It was an urgent situation, but I still got a chance to take a picture of the replica, and also discovered the reason why it felt so off-putting.

spans.text: It was an urgent situation, but I still got a chance to take a picture of the replica, and also discovered the reason why it felt so off-putting.

units.rawText: Persicaria, you mentioned that this kind of Entropic program reads the target's memory and morphs into another's appearance, right? Then, do they prioritize the appearance that's most familiar in the memory?
units.displayText: Persicaria, you mentioned that this kind of Entropic program reads the target's memory and morphs into another's appearance, right? Then, do they prioritize the appearance that's most familiar in the memory?

spans.text: Persicaria, you mentioned that this kind of Entropic program reads the target's memory and morphs into another's appearance, right? Then, do they prioritize the appearance that's most familiar in the memory?

units.rawText: Yes, but the appearance in the memory is not going to be the same as the real one. They can't be 100% perfect with their replication from the start, but they will continue to mimic every detail until they reach perfection.
units.displayText: Yes, but the appearance in the memory is not going to be the same as the real one. They can't be 100% perfect with their replication from the start, but they will continue to mimic every detail until they reach perfection.

units.rawText: ...I see. That explains it then.

spans.text: ...I see. That explains it then.

units.displayText: You two, take a look into the eyes of the replica.

units.displayText: That's odd... Why is her eye color different from mine?

spans.text: That's odd... Why is her eye color different from mine?

units.rawText: Unless...
units.displayText: Unless...

spans.text: Unless...

units.displayText: ...Hmm. Unless that's the eye color Sangoma had in my memory.

spans.text: ...Hmm. Unless that's the eye color Sangoma had in my memory.

units.rawText: Eh?
units.displayText: Eh?

spans.text: Eh?
